verdict.rationale: Both refactors centralize the email, name and role checks and keep the messages, their order and the per-handler differences intact. A also brings inviteUser's email handling in line with docs/api.md, which says invitation emails are stored lowercase, and adds a test for it. It reports this as a deliberate behavior change. B keeps the documented bug by adding a `lowercase: false` option to the shared validator, so a rule that clients rely on stays split across handlers, which works against the goal of the task. B is the more conservative refactor and flags the bug honestly, but leaving a contract violation in place behind a shared option makes A the better merge.
a_issues: Bundles a behavior change (lowercasing invite emails) into a refactor; it is documented and tested, but it widens the scope
No direct tests for the new validation.js, so boundaries such as the 80-character limit and a blank name in updateUser are not covered
Has two name validators (validateName and validateOptionalName) where one with a flag would do
b_issues: Adds a `lowercase: false` option whose only purpose is to keep behavior that contradicts docs/api.md, so the email rule is still not fixed in one place
Adds no tests at all, including none for the new module
The report's "16 existing tests" counts test/helpers.js as a test without saying so

verdict.rationale: Both changes correctly centralize the email, name and role checks while keeping the message order and wording. B also fixes the inviteUser email lowercasing, which docs/api.md explicitly requires, so the shared validator has no bug-preserving option. B discloses that change clearly and adds a test for it. A is a stricter pure refactor and flags the bug honestly, but its `lowercase: false` option keeps a known contract violation alive in the shared module, which works against the goal of fixing validation in one place.
a_issues: Adds a `lowercase: false` option to the shared validateEmail only to keep a documented bug (invitation emails must be stored lowercase), so case-insensitive duplicate detection for invites stays broken.
No tests added for the new validation module or the refactored paths.
The collectResults doc comment ('Runs each [field, result] pair... Skips nothing') is slightly misleading, since it receives results that were already computed.
b_issues: Changes inviteUser behavior (lowercasing the email) inside what was asked to be a refactor. The change is disclosed and justified by the docs, but it is still beyond the strict scope.
INVITABLE_ROLES stays in inviteUser.js instead of moving into the shared module next to ROLES, so the role lists are still split.
No direct boundary tests for validation.js, such as the 80-character limit or a blank name on update; the report acknowledges this.
